clue.text: Guide said a great deal about art

indicators.note: said tells us the word for a great deal is to be heard, not read, so its spelling may change

parts.note: loads means a great deal, as in loads of money

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the next word are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone tells us that a guiding figure talked at length on the subject of art.
explanation.walkthrough: LOADS spoken sounds like LODES; 'about' rearranges ART into TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A star used for steering by, especially the Pole Star, is a navigator's guide, and figuratively any guiding principle.

clue.text: Core of expedition is a long way off

indicators.note: the core is what remains when the outer layer is stripped, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, especially to watch or hunt animals in Africa

explanation.surface: The central point of a trip is somewhere distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' is not stripped as printed: think of SAFARI first, then remove its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at or to a great distance, as in seen from far away.

clue.text: The position of most of 17 ends up precarious

indicators.note: most of means nearly all of the word, so its tail is cut off

parts.note: 17 points to the answer of 17 across, an Act of Parliament

indicators.note: ends up means finishes, so only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A legal position based on part of an Act turns out to be shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is STATUTE; dropping its last two letters leaves STATU.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or rank in society or an organisation is one's position relative to others.

clue.text: Copies editions of a tabloid newspaper

definitions.meaning: as a verb, reflects or imitates exactly
the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid, and its issues are informally called this

explanation.surface: Duplicates are made of issues of a popular paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a long-running British tabloid daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect is to copy an image exactly; the plural also names issues of the Mirror tabloid.

clue.text: Model usually having points to teach class

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them a skill
a set is a class or group of pupils of similar ability

explanation.surface: A teacher's model lesson usually has key points to put across to the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are not ideas in a lesson but the movable rails that switch a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy railway is a scale model whose track normally includes switching rails called points.

clue.text: Tidy up after shattering into pieces

indicators.note: breaking something into pieces scatters it, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clearing up the mess after something has broken into fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' looks like part of the story, but it is the fodder for 'into pieces'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order or make neat is to tidy up a room or a desk.

clue.text: Poet gives small flower to sweetheart

parts.note: in crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river, and a small river is a brook
the heart, the middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A poet presents a little bloom to his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite for a river; the heart of 'sweet' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was an English war poet, famous for The Soldier.

clue.text: Matter thrown up at union conference — only half start talking it over

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its front five letters
the start of the word is its first letter
over means turned over, so the two letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: At a trade union conference, only half the delegates begin discussing the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' means a wedding; 'over' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are tossed over a couple after their marriage.

clue.text: Going round to the club

definitions.meaning: revolving or turning about an axis
... International, the service club for business people

explanation.surface: Heading off on one's rounds to the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating motion is going round; the Rotary Club is the well-known worldwide service organisation.

clue.text: One expecting to hear broadcast

indicators.note: to hear means the word is listened to, so a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Someone waiting to listen to a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in line to inherit is expecting a title or estate when the holder dies.

clue.text: He finishes off period at school in a history module

parts.note: a school year is divided into terms
taken as written

indicators.note: a module is one unit or section of a larger whole, so only a central section of the word is kept and its outer letters go

parts.note: the word history itself is the source, cut down to its central section

explanation.surface: A student wraps up a term of history coursework.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats 'module' as a section lifted from the middle of 'history'; the blogger found this loose, and it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings things to an end, or kills, is a finisher, as in the film killer robot.

clue.text: Loses control of fair elements

definitions.meaning: an aircraft or engine that stops working properly loses control
booths and stands at a fair or market

explanation.surface: Someone gets carried away at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine or plane suddenly failing does this; the plural noun names the booths at a fairground.

clue.text: Gabby to see dodgy doctor shortly to get recovery notes

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a quack is a fraudulent or unqualified doctor
IOUs are written notes of debt, held so the money can be recovered

explanation.surface: A chatty patient visits a shady medic who quickly provides sick notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovery notes' looks like medical certificates, but they are IOUs; 'shortly' trims QUACK to QUAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a talkative person who chatters endlessly.

clue.text: Gave up as fashion designer

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or form, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A clothes designer quits the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion designer' reads as one job title, but 'fashion' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job or accept defeat is to have given up, past tense matching 'Gave up'.

clue.text: Game and potato dish left unfinished

indicators.note: a dish left unfinished has its end missing, so the final letters are dropped

parts.note: a croquette is a fried roll of mashed potato in breadcrumbs

explanation.surface: A sporting event and a dinner of potato that nobody finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn sport in which players knock wooden balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Side first means to follow advantage

indicators.note: to follow means the word for means comes after the word for advantage

parts.note: an edge is an advantage over a rival
ways are means or methods of doing something

explanation.surface: A tactic of attacking from the flank to press home an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving with the edge foremost means with the narrow side leading.

clue.text: Act to get figure with a modicum of truth in it

indicators.note: in it means one piece is placed inside the figure

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted figure

indicators.note: a modicum is a tiny amount, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Behaving so as to look like a statue with a grain of honesty about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Ian treks out to part of the Eastern Cape

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man named Ian hikes out into the South African countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A former homeland in South Africa, now within Eastern Cape province.
explanation.definitionFit: This region was a nominally independent black homeland under apartheid, now absorbed into the Eastern Cape.

clue.text: A study starts off making assumptions for growth

parts.note: a den is a private room for working, a study

indicators.note: the starts of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A piece of research begins by making assumptions about how things develop.
explanation.definitionFit: A benign tumour of glandular tissue is a kind of abnormal growth.

clue.text: Driven mad by half-hearted performance getting cooker installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece goes into another
the heart of the word is its middle pair of letters, and half of them is taken away

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged by a weak job of fitting a new oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one E from DEED, leaving DED, into which RANGE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made insane or wildly disturbed in mind is being driven to madness.

clue.text: Return to island after directions make it possible

indicators.note: after means the reversed island follows the directions

parts.note: E and N are the compass directions east and north

indicators.note: return means go back, so the island's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Following directions back to an island allows something to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow or empower something to happen is to make it achievable.

clue.text: Princess has limits to awful temper

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal, sister of King Charles

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A royal whose bad mood goes only so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like mood, but here it is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat and slowly cool metal or glass toughens it, which is what tempering does.

clue.text: Take on an amount in rough sea

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a sum of money out onto stormy waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an amount' is the leaf here: the 'an' is part of the phrase rather than a separate A.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or responsibility is to adopt it, as in assuming command.

clue.text: Sticks with wave power

parts.note: wands that wizards wave to cast spells; the surface suggests tidal energy

explanation.surface: Something that adheres to the idea of energy from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave power' suggests renewable energy, but these sticks gain power when waved.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's or wizard's rods work their spells when flourished in the air.

clue.text: It enables travellers to overtake on the left

parts.note: to pass a car is to overtake it
port is the left side of a ship facing forward

explanation.surface: A road safety note about overtaking on the left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: An official travel document lets its holder cross international borders.

clue.text: See 24 across
Weather forecast could change by the end of the day

indicators.note: change means the letters are put into a different order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The weather outlook may alter before the day is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast skies are a common outlook given by meteorologists.

clue.text: Recollections Otterden takes a little while to state without evasiveness

parts.note: Otterden is the setter, who refers to himself as me
mo is short for moment, a little while
RI is the postal abbreviation of the US state Rhode Island
the setter uses only the outside letters of this word, E and S

explanation.surface: The setter takes a moment to say plainly what he remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outer E and S of 'evasiveness' are used, a loose device; RI, Rhode Island, goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Recollections are things remembered from the past, plural like the clue word.
